body:
### Question


In my `pyproject.toml`, I had some upcoming "future" features
```toml
# pyproject.toml for 'private-package'

[project.optional-dependencies]
future = [
  "private-package-1",
  "private-package-2",
]
```

When I set up my workspace including the 'private-package' like
```shell
uv add --dev private-package/ --extra dev --extra test --extra future
```
... it installed the 'future' package from PYPI - a migration layer between Python 2 and 3 - certainly not part of my dependency tree.

When I removed the "future" extra in the workspace toml from 

```toml
[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "private-package[dev,test,future]",
]
```

to

```toml
[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "private-package[dev,test]",
]
```
and ran `uv sync`, both the "future" package and my private packages were removed.




Is that intended behaviour? It feels like a security risk. It still installed the packages listed under "future" in my pyproject.toml .

### Platform

Linux 7.1.6-201.fc44.x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.12.1 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
title: uv add --extra installs from pypi if dependency group is labelled like a public package
